description: The bar chart illustrates the performance gain (in percentage points) of three large vision-language models—GPT-4o, Claude-3.5-Sonnet, and Qwen2-72B-VL—under two supervision conditions: “Strong Supervision” (represented by hatched blue bars) and “Weak Supervision” (solid light blue bars), as evaluated in the context of the VisuoThink framework for enhancing LVLM reasoning via multimodal tree search. The vertical y-axis, labeled “Performance Gain (+%)”, ranges from 0 to 30 with tick marks at intervals of 5. For GPT-4o, strong supervision yields approximately 24.5% gain, while weak supervision yields about 5.5%. For Claude-3.5-Sonnet, strong supervision results in roughly 9.5% gain and weak supervision in approximately 3.5%. For Qwen2-72B-VL, strong supervision achieves around 15% gain, and weak supervision about 5.5%. Across all models, strong supervision consistently produces substantially higher performance gains than weak supervision, with GPT-4o showing the largest absolute gain under strong supervision and Claude-3.5-Sonnet the smallest. The bars are grouped by model along the horizontal x-axis, with strong supervision bars positioned to the left of weak supervision bars within each group, and the legend at the top clarifies the visual encoding of the two supervision types.
